topic: Dissertation Literature Review: The Synthesis Matrix

copy.instagram:
Staring at 40 papers and feeling like your brain is about to melt? We’ve all been there—that 3 AM panic when you realize your lit review is just a list of 'Author X said this, then Author Y said that.' That’s a one-way ticket to a 2:2.

To hit that First-Class mark, you need to stop summarizing and start synthesizing. Think of yourself as a judge in a courtroom, not a librarian filing books. 

Swipe through for the blueprint:

Slide 1: The Trap – Why 'book report' style writing kills your grade.
Slide 2: The Fix – How to use a synthesis matrix to group by theme, not by author.
Slide 3: The Secret – Finding the 'gap' that makes your research actually matter.

Stop the endless reading cycles. Save this post for your next study session and check the link in our bio if you need a hand mapping this out.

copy.facebook:
Are you currently buried under a mountain of journal articles for your dissertation? I know that feeling—where every paper seems important, but you have no idea how to weave them into a coherent argument. 

Most students fall into the trap of summarizing authors one by one. If your lecturer’s feedback says 'too descriptive' or 'needs more critical analysis,' this is exactly why. To get that First-Class grade, you need to shift to thematic coding. 

Here is how to flip the script:

• Stop writing by author; start writing by theoretical debate.
• Compare the methodologies—where do their samples fall short?
• Clearly define the empirical knowledge gap that your research will fill.
